"""Product catalog used by the storefront.

get_product(product_id) -> dict    {"id": int, "name": str, "price": float, "currency": str}
update_price(product_id, price)    changes the price in the inventory service

Reads are cached in Redis (shared by every storefront process); cached
products expire after CACHE_TTL_SECONDS.
"""
import json
import urllib.request

import redis

INVENTORY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

_REDIS_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
_REDIS_PORT = 6379

# One module-level connection pool shared by all users of this process; it is
# process-local only (Redis itself is what makes the cache shared).
_pool = redis.ConnectionPool(
    host=_REDIS_HOST,
    port=_REDIS_PORT,
    db=0,
    decode_responses=True,
    socket_timeout=2,
    socket_connect_timeout=2,
    health_check_interval=30,
)
_r = redis.Redis(connection_pool=_pool)

# How long a cached product stays valid.
CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 300


def _key(product_id: int) -> str:
    """Redis key under which a product is cached."""
    return f"product:{int(product_id)}"


def get_product(product_id: int) -> dict:
    pid = int(product_id)
    key = _key(pid)

    try:
        cached = _r.get(key)
    except redis.RedisError:
        cached = None
    if cached is not None:
        return json.loads(cached)

    # Cache miss: fetch from the inventory service, then cache it.
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{pid}", timeout=10) as resp:
        product = json.load(resp)

    try:
        _r.set(key, json.dumps(product), ex=CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)
    except redis.RedisError:
        pass  # serving uncached data is better than failing on a cache error
    return product


def update_price(product_id: int, price: float) -> None:
    body = json.dumps({"price": price}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{int(product_id)}",
        data=body,
        method="PUT",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
        resp.read()

    # The inventory service has the new price, so any cached copy (in this or
    # any other process) is stale: drop it so the next read refetches.
    try:
        _r.delete(_key(product_id))
    except redis.RedisError:
        pass
EOF

import sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "/app")
import catalog

role = sys.argv[1]

def gets():
    return [l for l in open("/var/log/upstream/requests.log").read().split("\n") if l.startswith("GET")]

if role == "PHASE1":  # 10 processes, disjoint products, 5 reads each
    ids = [int(x) for x in sys.argv[2].split(",")]
    for r in range(5):
        for i in ids:
            assert catalog.get_product(i)["id"] == i
    sys.exit(0)

if role == "PHASE2":  # different process re-reads everything: must be 100% cache hits
    for i in range(1, 51):
        assert catalog.get_product(i)["id"] == i
    n = len(gets())
    print(f"phase2 (fresh process, 50 reads): upstream GETs total = {n}")
    assert n == 50, f"expected still 50 (all served from Redis), got {n}"
    print("PASS: second process served entirely from shared Redis cache")
    sys.exit(0)

if role == "PHASE3":  # update in one process, verify in others
    mode = sys.argv[2]
    if mode == "update":
        catalog.update_price(3, 999.99)
        p = catalog.get_product(3)          # this same process must see the new price
        assert p["price"] == 999.99, p
        print("updater sees new price immediately:", p["price"])
        sys.exit(0)
    # readers: separate processes, must see the new price WITHOUT an upstream refetch
    before = len([l for l in gets() if l.split()[1] == "3"])
    for r in range(3):
        p = catalog.get_product(3)
        assert p["price"] == 999.99, p
    time.sleep(0.3)
    after = len([l for l in gets() if l.split()[1] == "3"])
    print(f"reader sees 999.99; upstream GETs of product 3 {before}->{after}")
    assert before == after == 1, (before, after)
    print("PASS: cross-process readers get new price from cache, no upstream hit")
    sys.exit(0)

import sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "/app")
import catalog

mode = sys.argv[1]

def gets3():
    return [l for l in open("/var/log/upstream/requests.log").read().split("\n")
            if l.startswith("GET 3 ")]

if mode == "update":
    catalog.update_price(3, 999.99)
    p = catalog.get_product(3)
    assert p["price"] == 999.99, p
    print("updater: next read in same process returns new price:", p["price"])
    sys.exit(0)

if mode == "read":
    before = len(gets3())
    for _ in range(3):
        p = catalog.get_product(3)
        assert p["price"] == 999.99, p
    time.sleep(0.3)
    after = len(gets3())
    assert before == after, (before, after)
    print(f"reader proc: sees 999.99 from cache; upstream GETs of product 3 {before}->{after} (no new fetch)")

if mode == "ttl":
    # a fresh read must carry a ~300 s TTL in Redis
    p = catalog.get_product(11)
    ttl = int(sys.argv[2])
    print(f"TTL on product:11 key after read: {ttl}s (expect ~300)")
    assert 295 < ttl <= 300, ttl

if mode == "expiry":
    # prove expiry actually evicts: shrink TTL to 2s, read, wait past it, read again
    catalog.CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 2
    t0 = time.time(); p1 = catalog.get_product(13); t1 = time.time()
    time.sleep(2.5)
    t2 = time.time(); p2 = catalog.get_product(13); t3 = time.time()
    print(f"first read {(t1-t0)*1000:.0f}ms (miss->upstream), re-read after expiry {(t3-t2)*1000:.0f}ms (miss again)")
    assert (t3 - t2) > 0.25, "expected second read to hit upstream after expiry"
    print("PASS: cached product expired and was refetched")
EOF
